title: Privacy-aware aggregation layer for per-request inference metrics
creator: Priya Kaur
description:
Summary:
Build a privacy-aware aggregation layer in the metrics pipeline that enables accurate per-model and per-route inference KPIs while removing or obfuscating tenant-identifying request-level fields. This layer will sit between OTLP ingestion and Prometheus rollups (and downstream KPI exporters) and provide tunable aggregation and privacy guarantees (k-anonymity / differential-privacy modes).

Background & motivation:
- Current ingestion retains high-cardinality labels (caller_id, trace_id, request_id fragments) that are useful for attribution but increase privacy risk and cardinality explosion in Prometheus.
- Large customers in regulated industries require assurances that exported telemetry cannot be used to reconstruct per-request sequences tied to a tenant.
- We need a solution that preserves signal for inference KPIs (p99 latency, token-per-request, error rates) across model/route combinations while reducing cardinality and risk.

Goals:
- Provide aggregation primitives (time-windowed coalescing, cohort hashing, count+sum rollups) with optional differential privacy noise or k-anonymity enforcement.
- Emit Prometheus-friendly metrics (histogram summaries, counters with controlled label sets) and OTLP envelopes for downstream stores without leaking raw identifiers.
- Configurable per-tenant and per-route policies (sampling, min-cohort-size, DP epsilon, label allowlist).
- Integrate with existing metric-gateway and trace-linker components so latency attribution remains accurate for SLI computation.

Design notes (high-level):
- Placement: metric-gateway (ingest tier) will forward OTLP metrics to aggregation layer. Aggregator maintains short in-memory windows (default 30s) for coalescing and cohorting.
- Cohorting: canonicalize sensitive labels (caller_id, ip_hash) via prefix-preserving salted hashing; maintain ephemeral cohorts keyed by (model, route, time_bucket, cohort_hash). Cohorts below min_size are merged into an "unattributed" bucket.
- Privacy modes: "masking" (strip sensitive labels), "k-anon" (enforce min cohort size), "dp" (add calibrated Laplacian/Gaussian noise to counts/histogram buckets). Operator chooses mode per tenant.
- Export: produce low-cardinality metrics for Prometheus (e.g., inference_request_total{model=...,route=...,cohort=~"[a-f0-9]{8}|unattributed"}) and OTLP summaries for long-term analytics. Maintain mapping metadata (no reverse-map kept) for auditing.
- Performance: implement hot-path in Rust, use lock-free bucket maps and periodic flushes to reduce CPU overhead. Prefilter low-impact metrics to avoid churn.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end pipeline in testbed with synthetic workload demonstrates >= 95% fidelity for p50/p90/p99 comparisons with baseline for cohorts >= min_size, while reducing unique label cardinality by >= 70%.
- Benchmarked CPU and memory overhead per 10k rps does not exceed current metric-gateway by more than 20%.
- Config UI in Console to toggle privacy mode per-tenant exists (design prototype approved).
- Security review completed and DP parameter defaults approved by compliance.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature flag behind telemetry-privacy gate; default off.
2) Internal beta with non-production tenants for 2 weeks; gather signal and tweak DP params.
3) Gradual enablement for small set of customers (opt-in) and gather business feedback.
4) Post-mortem and metrics dashboard for privacy effectiveness and KPI fidelity.

Alternatives considered:
- Client-side hashing/obfuscation: pushes burden to customers and breaks multi-tenant SLI; rejected.
- Heavy reliance on Prometheus relabeling: insufficient for DP and cross-window cohorting; rejected.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: DP noise may obscure regressions for small cohorts. Mitigation: fallback to canary-specific sampling and alerting when cohort sizes below threshold.
- Risk: added latency on metric ingestion path. Mitigation: async flush, non-blocking ingest, and capacity autoscaling for gateway.

Open questions:
- Default epsilon for DP: recommend 1.0 for counts but need compliance sign-off.
- How to represent 'unattributed' in downstream dashboards without misrepresenting per-tenant SLA numbers?

- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/482

comments: 2026-02-24 - Priya Kaur: Initial scoping and stakeholder sync with Compliance and Platform SRE. Compliance asked for DP-first approach; SRE warned about memory blowup for high-cardinality models.

2026-02-28 - Ethan Morales: Prototype cohort hashing implemented (prefix-salted sha256 truncated to 64 bits) and microbenchmarks attached to PR #482. Observed 12% CPU increase at 5k rps; within acceptable range so far.

2026-03-03 - Data Science (review): Requested histogram bucketing preservation for token counts; recommended exposing both approximate histograms (DP) and exact aggregated metrics for cohorts above a high-confidence threshold.
2026-03-06 - Security (review): Requested formal threat model and to default DP mode to off until parameters are audited. Added action item for security_review_required.
